name: Diamond
colors: colorless to yellow or brown; fancy colors

name: Carbonado
notes: Mohs 10 is assigned as polycrystalline diamond, not measured. RI is empty because the material cannot be read on a refractometer. Only the density range comes from the GIA carbonado review (Gems & Gemology, Summer 2017).

name: Fancy sapphire
colors: violet, green, yellow, orange, pink, purple, parti-colored

name: Alexandrite
colors: bluish green in daylight, purplish red in incandescent light

name: Pyrope
notes: RI and SG are species-level values from Stockton and Manson (Gems & Gemology, Winter 1985), checked against the MSA Handbook of Mineralogy. The published RI maximum is an open bound (below 1.742), stored here as a plain value. Mohs is the garnet-group range.

name: Almandine
colors: deep red, brownish red, violet red
notes: RI and SG are species-level values from Stockton and Manson (Gems & Gemology, Winter 1985), checked against the MSA Handbook of Mineralogy. Mohs is the garnet-group range.

name: Spessartine
notes: RI and SG are species-level values from Stockton and Manson (Gems & Gemology, Winter 1985), checked against the MSA Handbook of Mineralogy. The published RI maximum is an open bound (below 1.810), stored here as a plain value. Mohs is the garnet-group range.

name: Rubellite
colors: pink, red, purplish red, orangy red, brownish red

name: Indicolite
colors: dark violetish blue, blue, greenish blue

name: Paraíba tourmaline
colors: intense violetish blue, greenish blue, blue

name: Amethyst
colors: light lilac to deep purple, often zoned
notes: Chapter 03 flags 1.544, the quartz RI used in its dispersion chart, as not confirmed on a fetched grade-A page.

name: Citrine
colors: yellow to orange to orangy red
notes: Chapter 03 flags 1.544, the quartz RI used in its dispersion chart, as not confirmed on a fetched grade-A page.

name: Rose quartz
notes: Chapter 03 flags 1.544, the quartz RI used in its dispersion chart, as not confirmed on a fetched grade-A page.

name: Smoky quartz
notes: Chapter 03 flags 1.544, the quartz RI used in its dispersion chart, as not confirmed on a fetched grade-A page.

name: Agate
notes: No grade-A source found. RI, SG and Mohs come from the International Gem Society, The Gemology Project or Wikipedia and should be re-measured or re-sourced.

name: Chrysoprase
notes: No grade-A source found. RI, SG and Mohs come from the International Gem Society, The Gemology Project or Wikipedia and should be re-measured or re-sourced.

name: Precious opal
colors: white, gray or black body with play-of-color

name: Jadeite
colors: green, white, yellow, reddish orange, lavender, gray, black

name: Nephrite
colors: light to dark green, yellow, brown, black, gray, white

name: Tanzanite
colors: violet blue to bluish violet to violet purple

name: Topaz
colors: yellow, orange, brown, pink to red to purple, blue, colorless

name: Zircon
colors: blue, red, yellow, orange, brown, green

name: Peridot
colors: brown-green to yellowish green to pure green

name: Turquoise
notes: The formula is the IMA-CNMNC one, with four waters. GIA writes it with five.

name: Lapis lazuli
colors: greenish blue to violetish blue, with calcite and pyrite
notes: Mohs (5–6) has no grade-A source; RI and SG are GIA’s. The formula is the IMA-CNMNC lazurite formula from redefinition proposal 20-H.

name: Malachite
notes: Values follow the MSA Handbook of Mineralogy.

name: Moonstone
colors: colorless to white, gray, green, peach, brown; blue sheen

name: Labradorite
colors: gray to dark with blue, green, gold flash
notes: Mohs 6–6.5 follows the MSA Handbook of Mineralogy for plagioclase. GIA’s own feldspar pages disagree with each other on hardness.

name: Sunstone (oligoclase)
colors: yellow, green, red, red-brown, colorless, with glitter
notes: Mohs 6–6.5 follows the MSA Handbook of Mineralogy for plagioclase. GIA’s own feldspar pages disagree with each other on hardness.

name: Apatite
notes: Values follow the MSA Handbook of Mineralogy (fluorapatite).

name: Sphene
notes: Values follow the MSA Handbook of Mineralogy (titanite).

name: Andalusite
notes: Values follow the MSA Handbook of Mineralogy.

name: Kyanite
notes: Hardness is directional: 5.5 parallel to [001] and 7 parallel to [100] (MSA Handbook of Mineralogy).

name: Chrome diopside
notes: Values follow the MSA Handbook of Mineralogy (diopside).

name: Fluorite
notes: Values follow the MSA Handbook of Mineralogy. Chapter 03 flags 1.434, the fluorite RI used in its dispersion chart, as not confirmed on a fetched grade-A page.

name: Painite
notes: Values follow the MSA Handbook of Mineralogy.

name: Taaffeite
colors: mauve to purple, purplish red, grayish violet, colorless
notes: RI and SG come from a study of ten stones, eight of them chromium-bearing, so the range may be narrower than the species. Mohs (8–8.5) is a trade figure with no grade-A source.

name: Grandidierite
notes: RI and SG come from the first faceted stone from Sri Lanka. A later GIA study of Madagascar material gives a density near 3.01, so SG may be low. Mohs has no grade-A source.

name: Benitoite
notes: Chapter 03 flags 1.757, the benitoite RI used in its dispersion chart, as not confirmed on a fetched grade-A page.

name: Jeremejevite
notes: Values follow the MSA Handbook of Mineralogy.

name: Serendibite
notes: Values follow the MSA Handbook of Mineralogy.

name: Pearl
colors: white, black, gray, yellow, orange, pink, lavender, green, blue

name: Amber
colors: yellow, orange, brown; rarely blue or green

name: Precious coral
notes: Values follow CIBJO’s Coral Book (2024).

name: Jet
notes: No grade-A source found. RI, SG and Mohs come from the International Gem Society, The Gemology Project or Wikipedia and should be re-measured or re-sourced.
